items.body: Home » Jazz Musicians » John Beasley CLAIM PAGE John Beasley Biography Articles News Press Teacher Has Influenced Pianist • Composer • Arranger • Producer • Music Director Two-time GRAMMY® Award winner and 14-time GRAMMY nominee (with two Latin GRAMMY nominations and an Emmy nomination), John Beasley is one of contemporary music’s most versatile and sought-after pianists, composers, and arrangers. Launching his professional career in his early 20s with jazz legends Miles Davis and Freddie Hubbard, Beasley quickly established himself as a dynamic force at the keyboard. Over the decades, he has collaborated with a wide range of artists, including Dianne Reeves, Sergio Mendes, John Patitucci, Chaka Khan, Christian McBride, and Carly Simon. As a music director, Beasley has helmed international tours for Steely Dan, A. R. Rahman (Slumdog Millionaire), and Queen Latifah, and served as co–music director/arranger for Chucho Valdés' La Creación tour. Recording Artist Beasley’s discography spans more than 20 albums, earning him two GRAMMY Awards and 14 nominations across jazz categories. His acclaimed big band project, MONK'estra, reimagines the music of Thelonious Monk and garnered six consecutive GRAMMY nominations, including a win. In 2024, Beasley released three albums, earning two GRAMMY nominations: Returning to Forever with the Frankfurt Radio Big Band (Best Large Jazz Ensemble) El Trio: Live in Italy (Best Latin Jazz Album) Butterfly Effect, a piano–saxophone collaboration with Magnus Lindgren His ambitious Bird Lives project — a reimagining of Charlie Parker’s music with the SWR Big Band and string ensemble — earned a 2023 GRAMMY Award for his arrangement of “Scrapple from the Apple,” along with three additional nominations. Beasley also ventured into Fado-jazz collaborations with Portuguese vocalist Maria Mendes, arranging and conducting the Metropole Orkest on Close to Me and Saudade: Colours of Love. Both albums received Latin GRAMMY and GRAMMY nominations, with Close to Me winning the Dutch Edison Award for Best Jazz Vocal Album (2021). In 2026, Beasley releases two major projects: Invisible Piano with the SWR Big Band, a commision of 5 originals and 2 familiar songs Unlimited Miles, a powerhouse sextet recording featuring Sean Jones, Kurt Rosenwinkel, Mark Turner, Ben Williams, and Terreon Gully — reimagining four decades of the music of Miles Davis. Music Director – International Jazz Day When UNESCO declared April 30 as International Jazz Day in 2011, Beasley was appointed Music Director for the annual global gala concerts presented by the Herbie Hancock Institute of Jazz. Since 2012, he has led all-star concerts in cities including Paris, Istanbul, Osaka, Havana, St Petersburg Melbourne, New Orleans, New York, Los Angeles, and Washington, D.C., and Tangiers, Abu Dhabi, with broadcasts on PBS. The 2016 “Jazz at the White House” gala hosted by President Barack Obama and First Lady Michelle Obama earned Beasley an Emmy nomination for Outstanding Musical Direction. The 2026 International Jazz Day celebration will be held in Chicago. items.body: UPDATED: MARCH 25, 2026 Biography Articles Born: July 3, 1979 Fascinated by the Piccolos of the Basel carnival, Ben Zahler picked up the flute at the age of eight. Yet, before he could switch to the Piccolo, he dived down into the world of Jazz clubs and never looked back. After attaining his “Master of Arts” at the Swiss Jazz School Bern with Andy Scherrer, Bert Joris and Günter Wehinger, he toured with his Band aloft (among others with Nadja Stoller and Stefan Rusconi) and recorded his first album We Do (TCB 26802). Other notable records include the Paul Klee record by the Swiss Jazz Orchestra directed by Jim McNeely. In the past years, Ben Zahler has been an active member of the Basel Jazz Scene, performing with various bands and also supporting the scene by organizing jam sessions and concerts. In this time, he has performed with rising stars in the Swiss jazz scene such as Yumi Ito, but also with established artists like Hans Feigenwinter. In 2015 he founded his new band Ben Zahler’s Songgoing, which has toured since Switzerland and Germany. The band plays with very few exceptions original compositions by Ben and the other band members. In November 2018, the band will publish its first album Quietly Cold (TCB 35902). items.body: UPDATED: JANUARY 25, 2026 Biography Articles Press Influencers Barbara Bruckmüller, a composer and jazz pianist born in Vienna, was influenced by the sounds of "Hollywood Jazz" from the 1930s, 40s, and 50s at a young age. Although she received piano lessons early on and studied intensively for seven years, it took some time for her to discover her true passion for jazz. She successfully completed her jazz piano studies with Paul Urbanek at the Gustav Mahler Conservatory in Vienna in 2004, marking the beginning of a remarkable musical journey. Barbara's inspiration and role models lie not so much in individual pianists, but rather in great Big Band leaders and composers such as Duke Ellington, Count Basie, Oliver Nelson, Thad Jones/Mel Lewis, Gil Evans, Joe Henderson, and Maria Schneider. In 2009 the debut concert of the BBBB - Barbara Bruckmüller Big Band - graced the stage at Porgy & Bess in Vienna. Yet, Barbara Bruckmüller's fervor for the orchestra remains as vibrant as ever. In 2013, she debuted her first album, "Barbara Bruckmüller Big Band," showcasing her original compositions and earning acclaim with the "Preis der deutschen Schallplattenkritik" (German Record Critics' Prize). Her subsequent release, a heartfelt tribute to her late mother, seamlessly fused traditional Viennese melodies with the infectious rhythm of swing, demonstrating her versatility as a composer and arranger. In 2015, Barbara assumed leadership of the Porgy & Bess Stageband series, orchestrating captivating performances that featured collaborations with spoken word artist Wadud Ahmad and live musical accompaniment to silent films, showcasing her ability to tailor her ensemble to diverse artistic expressions. Distinguished guests, including New York crooner Tony Hewitt and Austrian trumpeter Thomas Gansch, graced the Big Band stage, captivating audiences with dedicated evenings honoring the legacies of Frank Sinatra, Ray Charles, and showcasing compositions from female band members Viola Falb and Swantje Lampert. The Big Band boasts an ensemble of exceptional musicians, from trombonist Robert Bachner to Saxophonist Viola Falb of the Austrian jazz scene. International talents, such as the late Brazilian bassist Paulo Cardoso or American Pianist Danny Grissett contributed their artistry, leaving an indelible mark on the ensemble. Bruckmüller's prowess as a composer was further recognized in 2017 when she received a composition grant from the Austrian Federal Chancellery, solidifying her place as a luminary in the contemporary jazz landscape. Supported by this grant from the BMUKK, Barbara expanded the Big Band into a full-fledged jazz orchestra, augmenting its sound with strings for her ambitious compositions, "A Chain of Moments - Suite in Five Movements" and "¡MONKuKNOW!?" Her latest work, "The Spaces Within and Without," premiered in 2021. In 2022, audiences were treated to the electrifying energy of Barbara Bruckmüller Big Band live at Porgy & Bess, Vienna, with a vinyl release capturing the essence of their unforgettable performance from 2020. items.body: Pig Hurt People Hurt Metropolis Records Following a period of relative inactivity from around the release of 2005’s Pigmata through to 2016’s The Gospel, Raymond Watts has been releasing roughly an album a year, remix and reissue releases notwithstanding. It’s been a lot to follow to be honest, and while the initial rush of hearing the cult producer and performer back in the saddle, the quality and delivery of the material has been mixed, with some standouts, some comfortably fine records, and a few forgettable snoozers. With that in mind, 2026’s Hurt People Hurt is already fighting an uphill battle; even leaving aside very casual fans, Watts’ devoted fanbase have been trained to expect a few good songs, some filler and on average one quite good track, usually whichever one successfully pairs Watts’ powerful vocal charisma with a vocal hook and a solid riff. To be perfectly frank, Hurt People Hurt doesn’t totally buck that trend in terms of quality, landing firmly in okay-to-not-bad territory. That said, it does show Watts stretching beyond the chunky guitar, croon-and-growl groove he’s been working for the better part of the last decade. Opening track “Tosca’s Kiss” returns to some of Pig’s earlier stylings with it’s rush of creepy piano and some subtle production and arrangement touches around its gritty bass and downtuned chug, finding a nice middle ground between studio orchestration and live rock n’ roll power. There are a few other moments of equal strength here, such as the title track, which has a nice bit of western twang and a properly catchy chorus, with Watts in his classic camp evil cowboy delivery. “Scars” relegates the guitars to edges of the track, instead relying on a variety of squelchy and squealing synths and one of Watts’ most theatrical deliveries to great effect. Hearing him invoke his sleazy preacher persona on the stomping slowburn of “Ruins” reminds you of his tremendous charisma, and why he’s maintained a following amongst industrial rock fans for all these years. Sadly, there are just a few too many filler tracks in the mix, and while none of them is objectively poor, they do betray a reliance on just doing the cod-KMFDM thing (which ironically might still be better than most filler KMFDM songs these days) that has too often been a fallback for the project in recent years. “Quid Pro Quo” has moments of inspiration via the choral vocals and some fun horns and drum touches, but it all gets paved under by a dead boring guitars and a too weak chorus that flattens the song down when it should be getting its motor running. “Sex & Suicide” is about as chalk a song as you could expect from Pig these days, a decent little vocal melody on the chorus that can’t detract from the lack of substance behind all the sturm and drang in its delivery. Watts at least always sounds committed to what he’s doing on every track, but is sometimes sabotaged by a half-baked premise; see “Monkey See Monkey Do”, where he layers in some horrifyingly dated dubstep wubs, presumably to make a point about playing follow-the-leader creatively, a valid choice if those sounds weren’t completely absent from current music production. It’s a lot easier to pick out the lesser moments on Hurt People Hurt simply because in fits and starts it threatens to rise above the decent but unexceptional standard of Pig’s modern material, which makes its shortcomings seem more glaring. Speculatively, Watt’s high rate of output could potentially have contributed to the unevenesss here; if so it’ll be interesting to hear if the next Pig album takes a little more time to dial in what really works here, and spread it across the entirety of a record. Buy it. Hurt People Hurt by PIG The post Pig, “Hurt People Hurt” appeared first on I Die: You Die.
items._cn_summary: Pig乐队的《Hurt People Hurt》是一张延续Raymond Watts工业摇滚风格的唱片，整体落入中规中矩的水准。Metropolis Records发行的这张专辑在音乐表现上有可取之处，如《Tosca’s Kiss》回归早期风格并融入钢琴与编排层次，《Ruins》展现 Watts标志性的邪恶传教士人格魅力，《Scars》则以合成器为核心减少吉他比重。然而专辑整体缺乏实验性和创新意识，依赖程式化的KMFDM式工业套路，多首曲目沦为填充物，平淡的吉他编排与缺乏张力的合唱削弱了整体表现力。对于偏好实验/前卫或暗潮融合的用户而言，该专辑虽属工业摇滚范畴但创新不足，难以满足其对突破性音乐探索的期待。

items.body: STARGLOW debut the explosive and power-packed music video for their gritty and edgy single ' Good Boys Anthem '. The track sees them fully evolve into a more solidified and versatile musical direction as they infuse evocative lyrics with genre-blurring melodies to create interesting sonic textures. 'Good Boys Anthem' is built on a foundation of searing rock-inspired guitar chords with raw and abstract shoegaze melodies. The track depicts the fragmented emotions that bubble up within youths as they navigate the unpredictable path of life. Members TAIKI and GOICHI contributed to the writing process, offering an intimate and honest exploration of vulnerability, pride, and human connection. Directed by Hiroshi Shinagawa , the music video is set in an abandoned warehouse with a dark and almost dangerous buzz in the air. The visuals unfold like a gritty action film as STARGLOW take on a more cinematic style with this project. With fight scenes set in the rain, it tells the story of friendship, brotherhood, and loyalty between five friends who try to stick together despite the forces of adulthood and overwhelming responsibilities trying to pry them apart. The release of 'Good Boys Anthem' falls into place with 2026 being a particularly eventful year for the group. Their two MUSIC AWARDS JAPAN 2026 nominations under the categories Best New Artist and Radio Special Award: Radio Rising Artist of the Year, and the announcement of additional arena dates for their ongoing STARGLOW 1st Fan Meeting -STAR CRUISE- tour , including shows at Yokohama Arena and GLION ARENA KOBE , solidify their position as one of J-pop's rising stars to watch. With 'Good Boys Anthem', STARGLOW continue to push the boundaries of their artistry, embracing a darker and more emotionally charged sound that highlights both their musical versatility and storytelling ambition. As the group’s momentum continues to build through major award nominations, expanding arena shows, and increasingly cinematic releases, STARGLOW are proving themselves to be one of the most exciting rising forces in the J-pop scene today.

items.body: South Korean indie favourites JANNABI are finally heading to Singapore for the very first time. Presented by FriedRice Entertainment , the duo’s JANNABI 1st Asia Tour : Sweat & Stardust in Singapore will take place on 13 August at Capitol Theatre , marking the Singapore stop of the band’s first-ever Asia tour. Comprised of Choi Jung-hoon and Kim Do-hyung , JANNABI have become one of Korea’s most beloved indie acts thanks to their nostalgic chamber pop sound and emotionally resonant songwriting. Since debuting in 2014, the band have steadily built a devoted following through releases that explore themes of youth, love, and growth. View this post on Instagram A post shared by FriedRice Entertainment (@friedrice.live) The band are perhaps best known for their breakout hit ‘for lovers who hesitate’, which took home Song of the Year at the 17th Korean Music Awards in 2020. Their live performances have also earned acclaim for their immersive storytelling and distinct concepts, with their futuristic concert All the Boys and Girls 2125 winning the Grand Prize for Best Concert at the 12th EDAILY Culture Awards. Fans attending the Singapore show can also look forward to exclusive fan benefits. VIP ticket holders will receive priority entry to the standing pen, priority merchandise access, a JANNABI guitar pick, and a chance to win a signed concert poster. All ticket holders will also receive a commemorative postcard. Tickets go on sale from 2 PM (SGT) on 3 June via Ticketmaster Singapore .

items.body:
If you've just enjoyed the kind of (rare) sun-baked weekend as I have - DJing, dancing and wallowing in the natural wonders of an English forest - then this gorgeous downtempo number is exactly what the soul and body requires. We are delighted to host this premiere for two artists who come from different scenes but whose musical impulses contain a shared feeling of communality.

Based in the beautiful Devon wilds, Anna Ling is a class act. One of the new generation of alt-folk singer-songwriters, she has built a reputation as a mesmeric performer, composer, choir leader and lyricist. Anna certainly has audible roots in English folk traditions but she moves easily outside of them. Her contemporary and daring songs play and explore ideas of mythmaking, love and more, her voice an exceptional instrument as warm and enthralling as a campfire.

'Light', her sublime self-released debut album, arrived late last year and from it, Lucky Sun (aka Tom Lown) was asked to remix her 'Butterfly' track, his own live drums and synth embellishments revealing a chilled Balearic energy, a folk-infused downbeat groove shaped for the quiet, communal moments of a party. Acclaimed widely, he has returned to remix duties and has perhaps done an even better job on 'BTTFL' (Beauty To The Fading Light).

Reminiscent of the '90s backroom brilliance of artists such as Fila Brazillia or Kruder & Dorfmeister, Tom has straightened out the original song's 12/8 rhythm into a 4/4 'trip hop' groove and created an orchestral riff by looping Anna's ethereal choral harmonies. Instantly captivating, he then just lets the track breathe, lines from her full vocal appearing in dubbed out snippets, a violin is there then it's gone. So simple. So perfectly judged.
items._cn_summary: 这是一张独立民谣混音作品，Anna Ling的声音带有英式民谣传统，Lucky Sun的remix将原曲转为4/4 trip hop节奏，加入Balearic风格的电子元素和dub风格的声处理，整体风格舒适放松，具有一定的聆听愉悦度。混音技术成熟，将合唱和声loop成管弦乐般的纹理，配器简洁留白。作品偏向主流独立音乐范畴，与用户的实验/爵士/暗潮口味存在较大距离，创新性和跨界融合程度均属有限，未能体现强烈的前卫意识或独特的文化视角。

items.body: Review by Fercandio46 — Conceived during the tour for the previous album, Led Zeppelin's second volume is so distinct that it possesses its own autonomy. The approach is more direct, the sound is rawer, the songs seem tailor-made for live performance, and Page's growth as a riff-maker, one of his many facets, encompassing hard rock, blues, and soul, is gradually evident. However, certain litanies, remnants of psychedelia, can detract somewhat from the effectiveness, diverting the focus, as can be seen in "Whole Lotta Love" or "Moby Dick." These disruptions might be justifiable in a live performance, but in the studio version, they diminished the impact of gems that otherwise would have shone even brighter. Beyond this compositional observation, the band was at the height of its creative powers, brimming with ideas, and each member contributing their own unique touch.What Is and What Should Never Be breaks new ground, with jazzy undertones and a fusion of 60s British pop, blues, and funk... all within a song format, with Jimmy Page knowing when to glide peacefully and when to attack with deadly ferocity.Throughout Volume II, John Paul Jones's presence grows enormously, underpinning the foundations of the tracks until he becomes indispensable. Robert Plant had already developed his own style, making his voice another instrument and another flagship of the quartet's sound.The Lemon Song continues as a fundamental building block in what is constructed on this second album, where if it teaches us one lesson, it's that the blues is always something more, a vehicle to add elements and enrich the journey. And John Paul Jones's bass, which one can hear at times in addition to Jimmy's guitar, and the groove achieved were limitless.Led Zeppelin was always more than just good music. Unlike other bands on their contemporaries with similar characteristics, a certain mystical air gradually awakened within them, particularly in Jimmy Page, and that aura was transferred to compositions like "Thank You," music by Page and lyrics by Plant, an instant classic, almost like entering a chapel with muddy boots...guided by John Paul Jones' organ, before returning to the plea in "Heartbreaker," and another immortal guitar riff (not many can say the same). And fundamentally, there was that communion of the group, whose chemistry was at its best, those years when they were like an indivisible unit...recording together, traveling together, eating together, and that translated into the music.With "Living Loving Maid (She's Just A Woman)," they do whatever they want with time and rhythm, constantly changing them, making the song another example of instantaneous change within a song format, stretching and forever altering it. "Ramble On" will be a first approach to that electro-acoustic format that they will fully explore in Volume III, with Plant dressed in one of his many guises, and again the bass roving alongside the guitar, driving the rhythm of the composition. A funky, groovy drum rhythm that becomes Andean-like with guitars on the cliffs, with Page already playing his intricate parts that nevertheless seem simply enchanting in their placidity. And therein lies its charm!They could explode...and they could curl up in a corner...Bring It On Home closes a bluesy album full of contrasts, trying out different outfits and sharpening their weapons for the future...everything was here waiting for the moment to be used...but masters of the stage...lighting only what they wanted to be seen...the quintessence of a band that covered ground with an aerial perspective.
items._cn_summary: Led Zeppelin第二张专辑延续了硬摇滚与布鲁斯摇滚的传统框架，虽融入爵士元素和灵魂乐基底，但整体仍属主流经典摇滚范畴。乐评详细分析了Jimmy Page的riff创作、Robert Plant标志性的嗓音表现及John Paul Jones逐步凸显的贝斯/键盘编排，赞赏了乐队的化学默契与现场表演张力。然而在用户偏好的实验/前卫、电子、爵士即兴或暗潮等风格维度上，该专辑缺乏足够的实验性声响设计或跨类型突破，与用户音乐口味匹配度较低。作为1969年的历史专辑，虽具有开创性意义，但本质上属于传统摇滚范畴，与当代实验音乐语境距离较远。

items.body: Review by siLLy puPPy — HAIZEA (means "wind" in Basque) is one of the more recognized names when it comes to Spain's late70s progressive folk scene from the Basque region and existed from its formation in Hondarribia in1975 until its demise in 1980. The band released two distinct but vastly different albums duringthat time with this self-titled debut more in sync with the Basque folk revival scene that dominatedthe 1960s while the band's second release "Hontz Gaua" explored more daring experimental excursionsinto the world of electric psychedelic folk with much more complex arrangements. While the bandexperienced quite a few lineup changes during its five year run, amazingly the band's two albumsfeatured mostly the same members including vocalist Amaia Zubiria, guitarist / vocalist Xabier Lasa,bassist Gabriel Barrena and drummer Carlos Busto. This debut would be the only album for guitarist /vocalist Txomin Artola who would be replaced with flautist / guitarist Xabier Iriondo on the band'ssecond album.Prog lovers will probably find little interest in this debut as the band was still very much in thetraditional folk revival stage of the previous decade however with all the Basque musical flavorscorrupted by the experimental commingling of progressive rock and psychedelia imported from abroad,this debut does give a crisp clear glimpse into what the world of unaltered Basque folk actuallysounds like and that would be very similar to a lot of other European folk structures despite theBasque language and culture emerging as an anomaly isolate on a continent long overtaken by Indo-European tribes conquering the Paleolithic cultures. Obvious references on this lead to British folkacts such as The Pentangle or Steeleye Span however Basque folk sounds more similar to Celticflavors from not only Spain but the Breton region of France and of course Ireland, Wales and partsof Scotland. No bagpipes here though!While the second album was a crash course in how to update your traditions in the brave new world,HAIZEA's debut is the polar opposite of keeping things as authentic as possible with gentle folkrock instrumentation, a timeless atmospheric presence with all the tracks heavily rooted in the mosttraditional Basque folk melodies sounding much more like a Smithsonian Folkways release ofhistorical recordings than a so-called modern day progressive band but nonetheless the band performsbeautifully with a light airy feel that finds dual male and female vocals trading off along withgentle acoustic arrangements. While the the instrumentation is almost exclusively acoustic, snippetsof electric guitar do seep in on tracks like "Ura Ixurirk." The most notable different betweenBasque folk music and other European flavors is the strange rhythmic patterns that emerge from theband singing exclusively in Euskera, the native term for the Basque language.While this will not be considered essential for those seeking the more adventurous undertakings ofthe second release, this album is beautifully performed and for lovers of ethnic folk musicalexpressions i can't think of a better place to dive into the little known sounds of Basque folklorethan this debut by HAIZEA. The band's name which means "wind" really does shine though on this debutas the album passes by like a nice gentle breeze near the northern coast where Spain and Francemeet. Although there are few traces of anything progressive or experimental on this one it still isworth exploring simply as a point of reference as to how the Basque folk style was incorporated intothe context of prog rock and psychedelic folk from not only the band's sophomore release but themajority of other bands that were jumping on the progressive bandwagon after the collapse of theFranco dictatorship. The final track "Arrosa Xuriaren Azpian" at ten minutes with psychedelicovertones provides a vital clue to the band's next step. As an ethnic music lover i find this onequite pleasant as music like this is like a time machine that gives a glimpse into the collectivesoul of a culture even though i much prefer the good juicy experimental stuff!
items._cn_summary: 1977年巴斯克地区的传统民谣复兴作品，乐队HAIZEA的音乐根植于巴斯克传统文化，采用原声乐器编排，男女声交替演唱巴斯克语曲目。专辑风格接近60年代英国民谣复兴运动，呈现轻柔的大众化民谣摇滚气质，与现代实验/前卫音乐存在较大距离。虽然巴斯克语独特的节奏模式为作品增添了一定的文化辨识度，且乐队后续专辑转向实验性方向，但此张专辑本质上属于传统民谣记录性作品，实验性和创新性均较为有限，更适合作为民俗音乐研究素材而非实验音乐爱好者的聆听选择。

items.body: Review by martindavey87 — Black Sabbath's aptly titled 'Vol. 4' is the British metal pioneers' fourth studio album, and once again, it's another release that I struggle to really get into. I don't dislike Black Sabbath, I enjoy most genres of music and most bands, from any era. But for whatever reason, the stars just do not align because I just don't "get" the first few Black Sabbath albums. I'm sure there's a point, perhaps later in their career, where the band just clicks with me, but their first few records, often revered as metal masterpieces by fans, just do nothing for me. It's not all gloom and doom though (well, it kind of is!), as there are a couple of highlights. 'Snowblind' is a fantastic song, probably ranking up there as one of my Sabbath favourites, cheesy ballad 'Changes' has some great vocal and lyrics, and 'St. Vitus Dance' has some interesting guitar work. But overall, I find the rest of the tracks just seem to plod along, similarly to how I felt about their previous releases. I've tried and tried, and have had this one on my playlist for a while, but it's just not working for me. Perhaps I'll have more luck with their next album?
items._cn_summary: Black Sabbath的《Vol.4》延续了1970年代传统重金属风格，被归类为Prog Related类别但整体仍偏向硬摇滚路线。专辑亮点包括带有迷幻氛围的'Snowblind'、出人意料的抒情曲目'Changes'以及展示一定技术性的'St. Vitus Dance'，但整体编曲缺乏实验性突破，与用户偏好的实验/前卫/爵士/电子等方向存在显著距离。作为早期金属先驱作品，其历史意义不可否认，然而在当代音乐语境下，该专辑的创新程度和跨界融合度均有限，更适合传统摇滚乐迷而非追求前沿声响的听众。

items.body: Lola Amour celebrated a decade of music with a sold-out two-night anniversary event at 123 Block in Mandaluyong on 22 and 23 May , drawing over 2,500 fans across the weekend for a heartfelt full-circle celebration of the band’s journey. Originally planned as a one-night show on 23 May, overwhelming demand prompted the addition of a “Pre-Game” night on 22 May — with both dates eventually selling out. Across the two evenings, fans were treated to performances from Any Name’s Okay , Jan Roberts , Shirebound , and The Ridleys , alongside a career-spanning set from Lola Amour themselves. Beyond the live performances, attendees also explored the Lola Amour Museum , an exhibit showcasing memorabilia from the band’s 10-year history. Among the featured pieces were the band’s 2017 Wanderband Champions trophy, their Japan Ruby Award from the 2025 Music Awards Japan, and the iconic “Shiela” costume from the ‘Raining in Manila’ music video. The anniversary weekend was packed with memorable moments that highlighted the band’s close relationship with its fans and collaborators. One standout performance saw Sof of Any Name’s Okay join the band for ‘Clarity’, while a chaotic and crowd-pleasing cover of ‘Mr. Brightside’ brought together Jan Roberts, Renzo of Any Name’s Okay, Ivo Impreso of PLAYERTWO , and former road manager Peter onstage. During the set, bassist Manu crowd-surfed through the audience, earning one of the loudest cheers of the weekend. Fans also witnessed a playful moment during ‘Lambing’, where frontman Pio transformed into a human disco ball with a mirrored helmet during the song’s instrumental break. The emotional high point of the celebration came during a reunion of the bands that would eventually form Lola Amour. Former members Raymond King and Martin Kim returned to perform as Decaf , while current trumpeter Angelo Mesina briefly returned to his original role as drummer. Joxx Perez and Renzo Santos also made surprise appearances as Sinigang Na Baboy. To close the weekend, all former members joined Lola Amour onstage for the final chorus of ‘Raining in Manila’, creating a powerful moment that encapsulated the band’s decade-long journey from playing small venues to becoming one of the Philippines’ biggest acts. Part concert, part reunion, and part tribute to the community that has supported them since the beginning, Lola Amour’s anniversary weekend felt less like a retrospective and more like a celebration of everything still ahead for the band.
items._cn_summary: 菲律宾独立流行摇滚乐队Lola Amour在马卡蒂市123 Block举办十周年双日纪念演出，吸引了超过2500名粉丝到场。演出以流行摇滚为主要基调，穿插多支友队联合出演，设有乐队历史博物馆展览，回顾了乐队从2017年至今的发展历程。表演环节包括即兴合作翻唱、乐队成员角色互换等创意元素，现场氛围以温馨怀旧为主打，强调乐队与粉丝社区的情感连接。作为东南亚独立音乐场景的一部分，此次演出展现了菲律宾本土流行摇滚乐队的创作活力，但整体风格偏向主流流行范畴，未涉及实验电子、爵士融合或暗潮等前沿音乐元素，与用户偏好的实验性和跨领域探索方向存在较大差距。

The new Holy Pop! exhibition at Somerset House in London celebrates the world of modern shrines, “the objects and collections that honour heroes, celebrities, and cult icons”. The show includes extensive collections of photos and ephemera, carefully crafted sculptures, decorated crypts and inner city murals protected by Perspex. items.body: Review by A Crimson Mellotron — Kamelot is certainly one of the most enduring US power metal bands, known for a string of excellentearly 2000s releases and for their progressive-oriented and melodramatic sound. Their recent albums,however, tend to exhibit a dark and dystopian aesthetic that partially reminisces the music of bandslike Symphony X and Circus Maximus. Furthermore, many of their songs have great commercialpotential, and a large number of the songs appearing on 'The Shadow Theory' make no exception, whichis commendable. This is studio album number twelve from Kamelot, and third overall with Swedishvocalist Tommy Karevik, who has more or less become the face of this new era of the band. His voiceis really powerful, and his range is truly impressive, as heard on this very record.As for the album itself, it is a pretty standard-sounding proggy power metal album that combinesbombastic, pompous keyboards and orchestral arrangements with fast-paced guitars, technical riffs,and a strong propensity for memorable (and sometimes corky) melodies and straightforward songstructures. There is not much separating this album from the rest of the band's albums with Karevikas the lead singer, even though some fans have pointed out that this is not necessarily a bad thing.'The Shadow Theory' is a conceptual record, as the lyrics have a lot to do with sci-fi themes, whichis not uncommon for this band. Some key tracks here include 'RavenLight', 'Amnesiac', 'Static' and'MindFall Remedy', although the majority of the songs on here are well-written and well-produced.There is a melodramatic sheen and an indisputable energy that renders Kamelot's music ratherenjoyable. And with this in mind, 'The Shadow Theory' can be a perfect treat for someone who likestheatrical power metal with proggy bits and contemporary production. I personally find some of thewriting a bit shallow and predictable, as the record hardly introduces any new adjustments to theKamelot formula, but the overall impression I get is that of a really well-composed record.

items.body: Im Kino zu weinen hat etwas wunderbar Befreiendes. Erst mag es sich cheesy anfühlen, im Kollektiv die Tränen laufen zu lassen, doch irgendwann beginnt ein heilsamer Prozess. In Joachim Triers Familiendrama Sentimental Value hallte das Schluchzen unzählige Male von der hintersten Reihe bis zur Leinwand. Und auch Wochen später durchlebt man dank Hania Ranis Soundtrack diese Emotionen im heimischen Wohnzimmer noch einmal. Aufgenommen in den ikonischen Abbey Road Studios und in der originalen Filmlocation des Familienhauses in Oslo, erzählen die zehn Pianostücke die berührende Geschichte ihrer zerrütteten Figuren auf zarte und unpathetische Weise. Während Musik und Charaktere im Film beinahe miteinander verschmelzen, rufen die nach den Protagonist:innen benannten Kompositionen beim erneuten Hören klare Erinnerungen an sie hervor. So pirscht sich das Klavier in »Agnes« wie die ruhigere der beiden Schwestern leise und zaghaft heran und lässt einzelne Töne länger verweilen. Die akzentuierten Akkorde und nachdenklichen Pausen in »Nora« wiederum spiegeln die Zerbrechlichkeit und Ambivalenz der mit Lampenfieber kämpfenden Schauspielerin. Das ihr gewidmete Stück wirkt als Abschluss des Albums wie eine Versöhnung mit dem gemeinsamen Vater Gustav, der ungewollt ein generationenübergreifendes Trauma weiterträgt. Hörbar wird diese düstere Vergangenheit durch beunruhigende, ätherische Klänge, die wie ein eisiger Wind durchs Stereo ziehen.

items.body: UPDATED: JANUARY 3, 2026 Biography Articles News Press Born: March 11, 1958 Born and raised in New York and a graduate of New England Conservatory, Ricci has studied and performed and various styles of global music that he integrates with his jazz foundation leading to a brilliant career as a guitarist, arranger and producer in the USA and Brasil. From the 1980’s on, he has performed at some of the most prestigious jazz clubs in NYC sharing the stage or studio with many great names on the scene such as Michael Wolff, Dennis Irwin, Sonny Fortune, David Kikoski, Harold Vick, Victor Jones, Santi DeBriano, Mino Cinelu, Mike Clark, Bakithi Kumalo, Larry Willis and so many others in clubs such as Mezzrow’s, Fat Tuesday’s, Visiones, Birdland, Zinc Bar, Zanzibar, NuBlu, the Iridium and the Blue Note. In a November ’86 show at the Blue Note, Paul’s performance alongside the pianist Jaki Byard earned him a special mention in the New York Times by the noted jazz critic John S. Wilson who singled out his "...fascinating unaccompanied performance of Lover Man" He has also worked with many Brazilian artists in NYC including legendary drummers Dom Um Romao and Edison Machado, Luizao Maia, Mauro Refosco, Helio Alves and with vocalists Bebel Gilberto and Astrud Gilberto, with whom he also performed on tour in Asia and Europe as guitarist, arranger and composer. In 1991 in a tribute concert to Stan Getz at the Hollywood Bowl in Los Angeles, Paul accompanied Astrud Gilberto with an all star band of Roy Haynes, Gary Burton, Kenny Barron and George Mraz. In July ’93 he played in the famed NY Public Theater’s "Shakespeare In The Park" production of "Measure For Measure" starring Kevin Kline in a Latin Caribbean musical adaptation of the play resulting in a series of shows with the noted Latin jazz drummer Bobby Sanabria who has received multiple Grammy nominations for best Latin Jazz album. Ricci’s continued musical curiosity led him from Brazilian and Latin music to African music. From 1993-1997, he was part of the African Blue Note band led by veteran drummer Jo-Jo Kuo which in addition to being a fixture in NY`s jazz clubs also accompanied noted African recording artists such as Coumba Sidibe and Sekouba Kandia Kouyate in their NY Concerts. His experience with Caribbean and African music led to an important 1995 European tour with singer and activist Harry Belafonte. To this day he is part of the Belafonte Alumni Band that has performed in the NY’s iconic Town Hall in commemoration of Belafonte’s work. He appears on over 30 albums as a sideman, and as a leader he has released two albums on Fresh Sound New Talent: Songs, Hymns & Ballads Vol. 1 and Songs, Hymns & Ballads Vol. 2. Both volumes feature Jason Rigby on saxophone, Jon Cowherd on piano, and Jimmy Macbride on drums. Jakob Dreyer has performed with artists such as Steve Wilson, Jochen Rueckert, Mike Holober, Tivon Pennicott, and Manuel Valera, to just name a few, and notable venues he has performed at include the Carnegie Hall in New York City and the Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts in Washington D.C. items.album: “Imperfection is a starting point”: the APAC conversations leading festivals to a greener space
items.excerpt: EMC & Mixmag Asia’s Earth Night 2026 discussion brought together organisers & artists from Australia & Southeast Asia turning sustainability talk into real-world actionContinue reading...
items.body: On April 23, 2026, EMC and Mixmag Asia brought together festival organisers, artists and event makers from across Australia and Southeast Asia for Connect for Cause, an online session hosted as part of Earth Night, the global initiative led by DJs for Climate Action . What followed was one of the more practical and honest conversations the regional scene has had about sustainability. But first, the speakers. Vicky Keeler is the General Manager of Strawberry Fields Festival , a 15,000-person music, art and wellbeing event held on Yorta Yorta Country in New South Wales, now in its 16th year. Halim Ardie also joined as co-founder of Club Conscious in Bali, who recently served on the organising team for Day Zero Bali ’s debut edition. Also on the speaker line-up was Phuong Le , Music Director of Wonderfruit ; the Thailand-based cultural platform that spans music, food, arts, wellness and architecture, drawing around 28,000 attendees annually and just celebrated its 10th year last December. Sydney-based DJ, producer and radio host Anna Lunoe also contributed to the conversation with years of experience in pushing sustainability practices directly within the artist and touring ecosystem. A consistent thread through the entire discussion was that sustainability does not require being a major festival or having a dedicated budget line. As Vicky Keeler put it: “There’s no step too small when talking about sustainability. It doesn’t matter what your scale is and what your influence is, but anything is better than nothing.” Phuong Le echoed this, pointing to a particular challenge in Southeast Asia: “The problem that we have here in Asia is just so immense, but you can still start somewhere.” The point being that the scale of the problem is not a reason to wait. It is a reason to act with whatever is available. From the artists side specifically, Anna Lunoe offered a reframe that cuts through a lot of the paralysis people feel: “Imperfection is a starting point and is something not to be shying away from at all.” Her own approach has been to treat sustainability the same way she treats any other part of running a music career, something to build systems around rather than add on later. Read this next: “The planet is our only dancefloor”: how dance music events are adapting to sustainability “Strawberry Fields have implemented so many different green initiatives over the years, and it’s definitely been something that has been layered over time as we’ve grown,” Vicky explained. She walked through one of the festival’s most significant changes: the introduction of a rewashable crockery system in 2019. It sounds simple, but in practice it meant building a cashless RFID deposit system from scratch, renegotiating with vendors, and running ongoing patron education campaigns…all without precedent in the Australian festival market. By last year, the system was saving an estimated 41,000 single-use items from landfill annually, and it now pays for itself. The lesson: a single sustainability initiative can touch every department of an event. “When you’re going to implement something like this, you know we went into it with open eyes knowing that we’re going to get pushback,” Vicky said. “You’ve really got to break down communication.” Halim Ardie’s experience at Day Zero Bali highlighted a different set of pressures. Working within a venue they did not own, with a 36-hour window to strike the site, and operating as a year-one festival in a market where sustainable supply chains are still developing, the challenges were structural as much as logistical. Read this next: Sustainable sesh: How clubs and festivals are boosting the green agenda One thing that worked: sourcing furniture made from recycled shipping pallets by local Indonesian craftspeople, who were then invited to the festival site to install their work. “That is a benefit and a positive impact on the ecosystem,” Halim said. The spend on furniture became community investment. “I think that the main thing is try to do as much as possible with what you’ve got. For example, if you’re buying the furniture, make sure that you can use recycled wood and if you’re doing that, make sure that you’re working with local crafts people that are within the community that could use this kind of high level of injection of money coming into them,” he underlined. At Wonderfruit, the founding ethos was sustainability from day one, and the team has spent years learning that systems which look clean on paper can collapse under real life habits: “Once you have thousands and thousands of people coming, you just realise behaviour becomes unpredictable,” she explains. Her example was the issue of single-use cups. Wonderfruit couldn’t just design a system and tell people what to do; it had to create a habit that felt natural. “We said everyone has to bring their own cup, or they can buy one at the festival. But if you don’t have a cup, you can’t drink. Which was actually a risk for us too, since we depend on bar sales. At the same time, you almost have to implement it radically for people to get it. Because once they show up without a cup and don’t want to spend money buying one, they figure it out: next time I’ll just bring a cup, and I’ll tell my friends to bring one too.” Read this next: Humans of Wonderfruit 2024 in their element The ultimate lesson? Accept that changes won’t work immediately. “It takes years to really embed these things. But you stay consistent, and the more people do it, the more others follow,” she concludes. The response has been to design for behaviour rather than enforce rules, and to stay consistent. Anna Lunoe spoke to what artists specifically can do, drawing on years of personal practice and industry advocacy. She stopped producing merch she couldn’t feel good about, stopped pressing vinyl she might not sell, and has spent years posting practical guidance online for other artists, such as on how to change your rider and how to book travel more efficiently. “One of the hardest things for me—both personally and in trying to influence other artists—was encouraging people to publicly acknowledge that they care about environmental issues. Because once you admit that publicly, you become accountable. I was really worried about opening myself up to that,” she shared. “It’s worth being aware of what you’re asking when you invite artists to go public about environmental issues: you’re asking them to have their lifestyle scrutinised. And so much of an artist’s life is difficult to align with sustainability; you’re working within an imperfect system from the start,” she explains further. Read this next: Hi DJs, we are Mixmag Asia & we would like you to adopt an Eco Rider What’s shifted her framing is something Halim Ardie also touched on, that is approaching limitations as creative prompts. “Talking about the creative side of sustainability and how exciting it is to find solutions that are not only more sustainable but so much cooler and more creative and more interesting and more inspiring. So that’s been my focus now in the way that I talk about sustainability; just life-hacking it and looking at really fun ways to make life more sustainable and more functional and just better in all the ways," she added. What emerged across the entire discussion was a set of principles that anyone in the scene can actually use. First off, start with what you control, and use it efficiently, whether that is 200 dollars or 200,000. A little can go a long way. Get the local context before building anything, especially in Southeast Asia where culture, rhythm and existing community relationships will shape what works and what does not. Support what already exists rather than building from scratch. As Anna Lunoe put it: “There are so many causes and initiatives already happening that desperately need your support. Put your energy behind the projects that are already happening that align with your values.” Read this next: Festivals in Asia to look forward to in 2026 None of this is perfect work; everyone on the call said so. But it’s real work, happening at festivals, in artist riders, in office banking decisions and in the people who build stages from reclaimed wood because it’s the right call. The combination of doing good and doing it well is exactly the kind of trend the electronic music community knows how to spread. If you'd like to Support DJs for Climate Action by making a donation, head here . Amira Waworuntu is Mixmag Asia’s Managing Editor, follow her on Instagram . Cut through the noise—sign up for our weekly Scene Report or follow us on Instagram to get the latest from Asia and the Asian diaspora!

items.body: The glitz and glamour of red carpet season rages on as the 52nd American Music Awards (AMAs) carpet receives some of the industry's rising stars and iconic legends for a night of recognition and celebration. This year's instalment of the awards spotlights more Asian artists, with several K-pop artists being nominated across categories outside of the usual Favourite K-pop Artist category . This year's awards feature two K-pop-specific categories, including Best Male K-Pop Artist and Best Female K-Pop Artist . The former category sees K-pop royalty such as ATEEZ , BTS , ENHYPEN , Stray Kids , and TOMORROW X TOGETHER nominated, with the latter category presenting an electrifying ensemble of the most fiery female groups, including aespa , BLACKPINK , ILLIT , LE SSERAFIM , and TWICE . Winners BTS However, Asian artists are not just confined to these two categories this year. This year marks a monumental moment with Asian artists winning among international nominees as well. Beginning with one of the biggest wins in a major category, BTS dazzles the crowd as their lead single ' SWIM ' from their comeback album ARIRANG won the Song of the Summer category. During their speech, RM shared, “Thank you so much for giving so much love to ‘SWIM’. When we made this album, we felt a lot of pressure and tried to figure out what kind of music felt the most like us right now. But the one thing we believed in was that we have to keep challenging ourselves and keep moving forward.” V then added, “To everyone out there who keeps swimming, we send you our love and support.” BTS accepts the award for Song of the Summer for "SWIM" at the #AMAs pic.twitter.com/UjTe8Lor11 — Variety (@Variety) May 26, 2026 Nominated against some of this year's most viral hits, like the shimmering allure of Harry Styles ' ' American Girls ', the sassy energy of PinkPantheress and Zara Larsson 's ' Stateside ', and even the haunting rhythm of Tame Impala and JENNIE 's ' Dracula '. That was certainly not the only time BTS would be on stage to accept an award, as they had a clean sweep, winning all the categories they were nominated for. They claimed their throne as the kings of K-pop as they won the award for Best Male K-Pop Artist. Rounding off their series of wins for the evening, they prove that they are not just a force to be reckoned with within the K-pop scene, but in the global music scene as well, claiming the coveted Artist of the Year award, marking a pivotal moment that reinforces their influence even after their temporary hiatus. RM thanked ARMYs once again for their support as he says, "...Our biggest thanks and gratitude always goes to ARMYs all over the world." Because of the fans, @bts_bighit is taking home the biggest award of the night! Congratulations on Artist of the Year at the #AMAs ! 🎉 pic.twitter.com/P9GJaZBpHV — American Music Awards (@AMAs) May 26, 2026 HUNTR/X (EJAE, Audrey Nuna, and Rei Ami) Soaring through more extremely deserving wins, the air went still as the nominees were listed for the prestigious Song of the Year category. While everyone eagerly awaited to know which song soundtracked 2025 and 2026, the crowd erupted into cheers as the empowering anthem ' Golden ' from Netflix 's KPop Demon Hunters emerged victorious. The Singing Voices of HUNTR/X: EJAE, Audrey Nuna, Rei Ami are your Song of the Year winners for "Golden" 🎶 #AMAs pic.twitter.com/6P1R5VnwFq — American Music Awards (@AMAs) May 26, 2026 ' Golden ' also triumphed in the beloved Best Pop Song category against an all-star lineup of nominees that included Olivia Dean , Sabrina Carpenter , and Taylor Swift . The bold voices of EJAE , Audrey Nuna , and Rei Ami also had their moment to shine as they took home the award for Best Vocal Performance . With 'Golden' having sparked a viral TikTok trend centred around attempting its legendary high note, their win in the category felt especially well deserved. Last but not least, after winning every category they were nominated in at the AMAs, the official KPop Demon Hunters soundtrack secured the Best Soundtrack award . Not only did the win highlight the film’s expansive global reach, but it also symbolised the continued growth of K-pop culture beyond borders as audiences around the world embrace its appeal. KATSEYE In the name of spotlighting global groups, KATSEYE stepped up onto the stage to accept their award for the New Artist of the Year category. During KATSEYE ’s acceptance speech, Sophia gave a heartfelt shoutout to BTS , thanking the group for inspiring them to represent their culture on a global scale. KATSEYE shouts out BTS for "inspiring us to represent our culture on a global scale" after winning Best New Artist at the #AMAs . (via CBS) pic.twitter.com/cDltrqc971 — Variety (@Variety) May 26, 2026 Known for their extremely vibrant and over-the-top visuals, KATSEYE also took home the amazing Best Music Video award for ' Gnarly '. "You could describe everything with one single word," and it would be awesome, as KATSEYE also had a clean sweep receiving the award for Breakthrough Pop Artist . Their wins are a testament to their rapid rise from their debut to dominating festival stages, and now winning awards with their explosive sonic style and undeniable ability to deliver hit after hit. TWICE One of the most monumental wins of the evening went to TWICE , who emerged victorious in the Best Female K-Pop Artist category. With their warm, lovable charm and confident flair, it comes as no surprise that the musical powerhouses clinched the award as they continue to carve out their own path and expand their artistry with each new release. Fans online rejoiced over the group’s win, flooding social media with congratulatory messages and celebrating the landmark moment. Iconic performances & moments The AMAs would not be complete without the reverberating beats of amazing performances. Select nominees staged amazing shows that got the crowd on their feet as they jammed out to some of the greatest hits on the charts right now. Needless to say, BTS delivered a powerful performance that served as a bold statement declaring, “We’re back, and we’re here to stay.” Still riding the high of their comeback era, they channel the passionate fire of ARIRANG , infusing their inner edge and rebellion as they opened the AMAs with ' Hooligan '. The striking track was the perfect way to kick-start the awards ceremony as its carefree nature was bound to spark excitement within the nominees and audiences. 📢 WATCH THIS WATCH THIS 📢 @bts_bighit goin' hooligan at the #AMAs Tune in NOW on @cbs and @paramountplus ! pic.twitter.com/l17LithXLp — American Music Awards (@AMAs) May 26, 2026 BTS also took the stage later to present SZA with her AMA for the Best Female R&B Artist. During her speech, she expressed that it was nice to officially meet the powerhouse group formally in person, sharing, "It's crazy that this is the moment, so I had to take this moment to just let this be the moment." SZA fangirls meeting BTS at #AMAs pic.twitter.com/m9ydMYVSxJ — Deadline (@DEADLINE) May 26, 2026 Later on during the ceremony, the crowd got their ' PINKY UP ' as KATSEYE strutted onto the stage, performing their latest hit single with its booming techno rhythm that created an exhilarating sonic atmosphere within the arena. The quintet blew audiences away with their energetic choreography, making their performance one of the most memorable moments of the awards. KATSEYE performed “Pinky Up” at the AMAs tonight and completely owned the stage. KATSEYE GOES WILD AT AMAs #KATSEYE_AMAs pic.twitter.com/wiMvNw0DZ8 — KATSEYE B✶SE (@KATSEYEBASE) May 26, 2026 These victories mark a huge shift in the industry as Asian artists are increasingly being recognised on global stages, proving that their music, artistry, and cultural impact continue to resonate far beyond borders. From electrifying performances to landmark wins, this year’s American Music Awards reflected a growing era of inclusivity and international representation within mainstream entertainment.

items.body: BABYMONSTER are officially bringing their second world tour to Singapore this November, and ticketing details are finally here. The K-pop girl group will perform at the Singapore Indoor Stadium on 28 November as part of the 2026–27 BABYMONSTER WORLD TOUR ‘춤 (CHOOM)’ . The upcoming show follows the success of the septet’s sold-out Singapore concert in 2025 during their debut HELLO MONSTERS world tour. Organised by Live Nation Singapore , the concert marks one of the group’s Asia stops for the ongoing world tour, which will also see the act perform across cities including Bangkok, Jakarta, Kuala Lumpur, Taipei, Hong Kong, Sydney, and Melbourne. BABYMONSTER are currently promoting their third mini album, 춤 (CHOOM) , which was released on 4 May. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Live Nation SG (@livenationsg) Ticket prices for the Singapore concert are priced at S$358, S$348, S$308, S$298, S$258, S$228, S$188, and S$168, excluding booking fees. VIP ticket holders will receive: Priority entry for standing or seated sections Access to the pre-show soundcheck party A commemorative VIP laminate and lanyard Limited-edition VIP gift Exclusive photocard set MONSTIEZ MEMBERSHIP holders can register for the Weverse presale from 26 May, 12 PM to 29 May, 11:59 PM . The Weverse presale will then take place on 8 June , from 10 AM to 11:59 PM . Mastercard and Trip.com presales will run on 9 June , from 10 AM to 11:59 PM , while the Live Nation presale is set for 10 June , from 12 PM to 11:59 PM . General ticket sales begin on 11 June at 12 PM via Ticketmaster Singapore .

items.body: Hans Zimmer is set to return to Singapore with his brand-new live production, Hans Zimmer Live – The Next Level World Tour 2026 , happening on 7 October at the Singapore Indoor Stadium . Presented by AEG Presents Asia , Semmel Concerts , and RCI Global , the upcoming show marks the legendary composer’s first performance in Singapore since 2019. Known for transforming film scores into immersive live spectacles, Zimmer’s latest production promises an even more ambitious cinematic experience, featuring electronic sound design, large-scale orchestration, spectacular lighting, and a brand-new stage concept. View this post on Instagram A post shared by AEG Presents Asia (@aegpresentsasia) Speaking about the tour, Zimmer shared: “I want fans to feel like they’re at a rave party or riding a roller coaster. For me, every show is a new voyage of discovery.” Fans can expect fresh arrangements from some of Zimmer’s most iconic film scores, including music from Pirates of the Caribbean , The Lion King , The Dark Knight , Interstellar , and Dune . The setlist will also feature selections from Dune: Part Two and F1®: The Movie . View this post on Instagram A post shared by AEG Presents Asia (@aegpresentsasia) The Singapore stop is part of Zimmer’s wider Asia run, which will also see the composer perform in cities such as Yokohama, Kaohsiung, Taipei, Beijing, Hangzhou, Chengdu, and Guangzhou. Tickets will go on sale via SISTIC on 2 June from 10 AM onwards.

items.album: Feeling Alright: The Complete 1975 Nancy Pulsations Concert
items.excerpt: We're super fortunate that this three-LP vinyl set consisting of previously unreleased material recorded live at the 1975 Nancy Jazz Pulsations Festival in France was released earlier this month...
items.body: We're super fortunate that this three-LP vinyl set consisting of previously unreleased material recorded live at the 1975 Nancy Jazz Pulsations Festival in France was released earlier this month as a limited-edition Record Store Day "First." Freddie King was in peak form and at the height of his popularity when the blues guitar giant and his crack band played to a huge, enthusiastic crowd at one of Europe's major music festivals at a time when audiences raised on rock 'n' roll began widely embracing those pioneering artists who were closely connected to the music's traditional roots. Thanks to album producer and archivist Zev Feldman, who sourced the recordings from the French Radio and Television Broadcasting Office, we now have a great-sounding live document of The Texas Cannonball — something that hasn't been very forthcoming in the past — performing a generous 16-song mix of his best-known instrumentals (including "Hide Away" and "Sen-Sa-Shun"), essential blues standards ("Got My Mojo Working," "Messin' With The Kid" and "Stormy Monday," to name a few) and covers of the late-'60s rock radio hits "Goin' Down" (by southern soul-rocker Don Nix) and "Feelin' Alright" (by Traffic's Dave Mason). Supporting King's stinging guitar lines and commanding vocals are simpatico touring band members Alvin Hemphill (organ), Lewis Stephens (piano), Ed Lively (second guitar), Benny Turner (bass) and Calep Emphrey (drums), a tight unit if there ever was one. The expertly paced program ranges in mood from calming blue-sky coolness to stormy rock intensity to see-the-light gospel ecstasy, the music leaving ample room for judicious soloing, stretching and testifying. The notoriously hard-living King died just a year after this performance, at age 42, a sobering bit of blues history that makes this deluxe package all the more valuable for today's listeners and collectors. Also available in CD format, it makes a great companion piece to this summer's poolside blues-listening.
items._cn_summary: 这是一张1975年法国爵士音乐节现场录音的重发专辑，收录Freddie King与乐队的16首演出作品，包括《Hide Away》等经典蓝调instrumentals及《Stormy Monday》等标准蓝调曲目。专辑为Record Store Day限定版黑胶，音效出色，具有历史文献价值。Freddie King的吉他演奏与演唱保持高水准，乐队配合紧密。整体而言，这是一张典型的传统蓝调现场录音，风格定位清晰但与实验、前卫、电子、爵士等当代前沿音乐领域存在较大距离，更适合传统蓝调音乐爱好者收藏。

items.album: Hear65's music video guide (May 2026) — Regina Song, SHIGGA SHAY, Mary Sue, Shye & Shohini
items.excerpt: When it comes to music, music videos are important supplements to what we can hear as they stimulate our visual senses in a way that sound cannot. From creative homemade projects to cinematic works that beg to be seen on a big screen.
items.body:
When it comes to music, music videos are important supplements to what we can hear as they stimulate our visual senses in a way that sound cannot. 
 From creative homemade projects to cinematic works that beg to be seen on a big screen, all forms of music videos are released by Singapore's talented musicians seeking to extend the stories told in their songs every month. In this monthly series, we will be rounding up the latest releases from our sunny island that might fly under the radar.  
 Check out  Hear65 's guide to local music videos for this month and contact us at hello@hear65.com to submit your music videos! 
 Regina Song - 'Your Charm' 
 Five years in the making, Regina Song 's latest bop was written about the thrill of unexpected attraction. Accompanied by this wonderful music video directed by Gareth Christopher , 'Your Charm' is one of her most playful and uplifting offerings yet, capturing both the giddy rush of a crush and a deeper celebration of individuality. "Honestly, this song means so much more to me than what it meant five years ago. Cause it feels like I let a part of my whimsical self come back. I’m finally getting back into my element," the singer-songwriter shared . 
 SHIGGA SHAY 西阁 ft. pH-1 & JP THE WAVY - 'OK CAN' 
 Built around a hypnotic saxophone loop and powered by multilingual bars, SHIGGA SHAY ’s new single ‘OK CAN’ sees the Singapore rapper link up with Korean hip-hop heavyweight pH-1 and Japanese trailblazer JP THE WAVY for a cross-cultural anthem that feels both effortless and electric. Blending English, Singlish, Mandarin, Malay, Tamil, Korean, Japanese, Thai, and French into one seamless exchange, the track transforms a familiar local phrase into a celebration of identity, rhythm, and connection across Asia’s hip-hop scene. Produced by longtime collaborator superjdoug, ‘OK CAN’ continues SHIGGA SHAY’s mission of bringing hometown stories to a global audience through bold, genre-bending sound. 
 Mary Sue - 'U Wish!' 
 Lifted from his upcoming album Rapihaler , out 19 June , ‘U Wish!’ sees Mary Sue keeping things stripped back and unfussy, letting the bars do the heavy lifting over a captivatingly smooth beat. Filmed at Malaysia’s The Spaceship , the no-frills visual captures the rapper casually performing in the studio, with simple lyric captions foregrounding reflections on trust, ambition, love, and inner conflict. It is intimate without trying too hard — less glossy music video, more late-night session energy, giving the track’s rhythm and thoughtful writing room to breathe. 
 Mary Sue - 'WALAO!' 
 We have Mary Sue yet again, this teaming up with Kuala Lumpur rapped Dametrill . Known for using a blend of Malay, Cantonese, English and Mandarin in his delivery, the mulilingual emcee joins forces with Mary Sue for a captivating track entitled 'WALAO!' . (For those unfamilar "walao” is a Singlish/Malaysian English exclamation with Hokkien roots, used when you’re surprised, annoyed, impressed, frustrated, or reacting strongly to something.) Produced by Atlanta-based underground experimental hip-hop artist feardorian , the song's surge-adjacent beat is a strangely a breezy complement to Mary Sue and Dametrill's Malay Peninsula slang. 
 Shye - 'In The End' 
 Serving as the emotional and melancholic centrepiece of Shye ’s sophomore album The Doves Came Home , ‘In The End’ drifts through shimmering dream-pop textures and towering shoegaze-inspired distortion with a quiet sense of acceptance. Drawing sonic inspiration from Cocteau Twins, Ride, and The Smashing Pumpkins, the track captures the fragile moment of realising that letting go is not a defeat, but a necessary step toward finding your way back to yourself. Anchored by Shye’s airy vocals and introspective songwriting, ‘In The End’ reflects the album’s lingering tension between softness and overwhelm, clarity and uncertainty — ultimately embracing the peace that comes with surrendering to the unknown. 
 Shye - 'If Today Was Yesterday' 
 Shye continues to unveil the emotional world of The Doves Came Home with ‘If Today Was Yesterday’ , a warm and wistful track about revisiting past versions of yourself with compassion instead of regret. Inspired by visions of sunflower fields and the quiet comfort of nature, the song pairs gentle reflection with hope, capturing the desire to “meet yourself halfway” and say the things you once needed to hear. Accompanied by a dreamy self-directed video, the track stands out as one of the brighter moments on the album, with the sunflower emerging as a symbol of resilience, forgiveness, and always turning toward the light. ‘If Today Was Yesterday’ feels like a comforting reminder to hold your younger self a little softer through life’s colder seasons.

items.excerpt: A review of Dr. John - Live at Rockpalast 1999
items.body: Live at Rockpalast 1999 documents a command performance at the Loreley open-air amphitheater by Malcolm “Mac” Rebennack Jr., aka Dr. John. Rockpalast is a live-music TV show broadcast since 1974 by Westdeutscher Rundfunk (WDR), the archival source for this CD-DVD package, and coincidentally a remarkable cultural institution on its own terms. Taped at the height of Dr. John’s international popularity, backing the singer-pianist-guitarist are New Orleans stalwarts Bobby Broom (guitar), David Barard (bass), and Herman Ernest (drums), a tight quartet that projects authority and engages the crowd from start to close. A striking UNESCO-designated World Heritage Site set, the Loreley is a slate pinnacle on a mythic horseshoe bend of the Rhine River, memorializing an enduring German literary legend both tragic and romantic. The setting is thus well-suited for Mac’s mystical spirit and lyrical style. By this stage of his career, he characterized his live show as a Mardi Gras revue with a mix of New Orleans standards and some of his most recognizable compositions.

items.excerpt: Explore Steve Wilson's biography, discography, and jazz legacy. Discover albums, articles, and interviews about Steve Wilson – one of jazz's most celebrated saxophone players.
items.body: Home » Jazz Musicians » Steve Wilson CLAIM PAGE Steve Wilson Biography Articles News Has Influenced Steve Wilson has attained ubiquitous status in the studio and on the stage with the greatest names in jazz. A bandleader in his own right, Jazz Times calls him the consummate saxophonist-composer and one of the finest alto and soprano saxophonists of our time. A musicians musician, Wilson has brought his distinctive sound to more than 100 recordings led by such celebrated and wide-ranging artists as Chick Corea, George Duke, Michael Brecker, Dave Holland, Dianne Reeves, Bill Bruford, Gerald Wilson, Maria Schneider, Joe Henderson, Charlie Byrd, Billy Childs, Karrin Allyson, Don Byron, Bill Stewart, James Williams, and Mulgrew Miller among many others. Wilson has eight recordings under his own name, leading and collaborating with such stellar musicians as Lewis Nash, Carl Allen, Steve Nelson, Cyrus Chestnut, Greg Hutchinson, Dennis Irwin, James Genus, Larry Grenadier, Ray Drummond, Ben Riley, Nicholas Payton, Orrin Evans, Ugonna Okegwo and Bill Stewart. In 2015 Wilson released his first project as a leader in 12 years, Steve Wilson & Wilsonians Grain: Live in New York: The Vanguard Sessions, on Random Act Records. Recorded live at the famed Village Vanguard in NYC on May 24 & 25, 2014, the recording features Wilsons potent quartet with Orrin Evans, Ugonna Okegwo and Bill Stewart. The CD was conceived to truly capture the live experience and the sound of one of the best listening rooms in the world. The tracking order reflects a Wilsonians Grain set, and includes three Wilson originals, and tunes by Orrin Evans, Joe Chambers, Thelonius Monk and Migiwa Miyajima. WBGO Radio describes Wilsonians Grain as jazz at its finest in conception, execution and spontaneity. He has recorded another project, Sit Back Relax & Unwind, for JMI Records that features Ray Angry, Ben Williams and Willie Jones, III just recently released. In the vein of the old CTI recordings, it is an analog recording and will be released a vinyl LP only. Produced by Steven Mandel (Music Supervisor the The Tonight Show with Jimmy Fallon, The Roots), he also contributed four tunes that were arranged by Wilson. There are two new tunes by Wilson and an arrangement by Ray Angry of David Bowies Space Oddity. Starting his formal training on saxophone in his native Hampton, Virginia, Wilson also played oboe and drums in school bands while performing in various R&B/funk bands throughout his teens. After a year-long stint with singer Stephanie Mills he decided to major in music at Virginia Commonwealth University in Richmond, where he performed and/or studied with Jimmy and Percy Heath, Jon Hendricks, Jaki Byard, John Hicks, Frank Foster and Ellis Marsalis. During those years he was also in constant demand for recording studio work, and as backing musician for touring shows such as The Four Tops and Sophisticated Ladies. Landing a chair with O.T.B (Out of the Blue), a sextet of promising young players recording on Blue Note Records, Wilson moved to New York in 1987 and the following year toured the U.S. and Europe with Lionel Hampton. Becoming a first-call choice for veteran and emerging artists alike, Wilson was the subject of a New York Times profile A Sidemans Life, highlighting his work with Ralph Peterson, Jr., Michele Rosewoman, Renee Rosnes, Marvin Smitty Smith, Joanne Brackeen, The American Jazz Orchestra, The Mingus Big Band, The Smithsonian Jazz Masterworks Orchestra, Leon Parker, and Buster Williams Quintet Something More. In 1996 he joined the acclaimed Dave Holland Quintet, and from 1998-2001 he was a member of Chick Coreas Grammy winning sextet Origin. items.body: C86 Holdings has acquired The Face from Wasted Talent Limited . In a joint statement released on 26 May , the Singapore and London-based announcement confirmed that the iconic culture publication will now enter a new chapter under C86 Holdings. First launched in 1980, The Face became a defining voice across music, fashion, style, and youth culture. The title ceased publication in 2004 before being relaunched by Wasted Talent in 2019 as a digital platform and quarterly print magazine. Wasted Talent is a global music and lifestyle media company whose portfolio includes Mixmag , Kerrang! , and The Face . The company describes Mixmag as “the global authority on dance music,” while The Face is billed as “the original home of style.” Kuok Meng Ru , Founder and Principal of C86 Holdings, said: “Some brands matter more than others, and The Face is undeniably one of them. I want to thank Ian and the Wasted Talent team for trusting me with the stewardship of this very special brand as it enters its next chapter. The work now is to carry its legacy forward with the care and ambition the brand deserves.” Kuok is also the Group CEO and Founder of Caldecott Music Group , whose portfolio spans BandLab Technologies , NME Networks , and Vista Musical Instruments . Ian Flooks , Chairman of Wasted Talent, added: “Meng is someone I've known and respected for many years. He has a rare combination of genuine passion for culture and a proven entrepreneurial track record of starting, relaunching and nurturing iconic brands, and evolving them for the future. I have every confidence that The Face is in the right hands.” For updates from The Face , visit theface.com .

Following two sold-out shows at Capitol Theatre in 2025, the American band are set to return with the 29 August stop of their For Lovers Tour at Arena @ EXPO . Known for defining the soundtrack of the early 2000s with irresistible hooks and singalong-ready choruses, the band’s upcoming Singapore show is expected to be their biggest one in the country yet. Fans can look forward to live performances of hits including 'Jenny', 'Just the Girl', and 'Catch Your Wave', alongside other fan favourites from across their catalogue. The Boston-formed outfit first built a massive fanbase across Asia during their original run, becoming one of Myspace’s most-viewed bands at the height of their popularity. Their 2025 Southeast Asia comeback tour reignited that connection with longtime fans, with tickets for their Singapore dates reportedly selling out within hours. As part of the For Lovers Tour , the band will also be offering VIP packages and experiences for concertgoers. items.body: Looking back on a glorious 11-year journey, the sun isn't setting anytime soon on SEVENTEEN as they celebrate their anniversary, sharing warm and heartfelt messages with CARATs on Weverse . Earlier this year, S.Coups , Jeonghan , Joshua , Jun , Hoshi , Wonwoo , Woozi , DK , Mingyu , The8 , Seungkwan , Vernon , and Dino all renewed their contracts with PLEDIS Entertainment , strengthening their bond with fans as they make a pledge to be their favourite idols for as long as they can. With many more milestone anniversaries on the horizon, CARATs celebrate this landmark moment by sharing clips of old performances and iconic moments that stay etched in their minds. As fans reminisce about the journey of the group so far, the members took to Weverse to share their messages of appreciation, joining in on the nostalgic reflection of the paths they've forged. Although he is currently serving his national service, Hoshi expresses his excitement to complete his duties and reunite with the band to continue performing and creating new bangers for fans to rock out to. The8 echoes a similar sentiment as he expresses his love by saying, "It’s been 11 years. Thank you for always being by our side, thank you to all the members for getting this far, it hasn’t been easy. Because of the time we’ve spent together, we've long become a part of each other’s lives. We hope to continue creating many more memories together in the future. Thank you for your unwavering love." As each member expresses their gratitude for the support from CARATs for the past 11 years, they look forward to an even more eventful future as SEVENTEEN. The group anticipates more new hits, even bigger performances, and new endeavours as they continue to preserve the original energy and passion that they have served up since their debut.
